question: What is the primary causative agent of tuberculosis?
explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which typically targets the respiratory system. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h1)

question: How is tuberculosis primarily spread from one person to another?

options.A: Through airborne droplets from coughs and sneezes
options.C: By direct contact with unbroken skin
options.D: By sharing eating utensils and drinking cups

explanation: Infectious droplets are expelled into the air when a person with active pulmonary TB coughs or sneezes, allowing others to inhale them. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary immune structure that walls off tuberculosis bacilli in the lungs?
explanation: The body forms a granuloma or tubercle to contain the bacteria and prevent them from spreading through lung tissue. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why do some people with latent tuberculosis eventually develop active disease?

options.A: Consuming too much dietary sugar activates the pathogens
options.B: Exposure to cold weather triggers the dormant bacteria to wake up
options.C: A decline in the body's immune defense allows the bacteria to multiply
options.D: The bacteria mutate into a completely different viral strain

explanation: When immune defenses drop, the containment walls break down, and the dormant bacteria become active and multiply. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which of the following is a classic systemic sign of active pulmonary tuberculosis?
explanation: Systemic symptoms like drenching night sweats, persistent fever, and weight loss are hallmark indicators of active TB infection. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h3)

question: A patient presents with a chronic cough for three weeks, weight loss, and blood-streaked sputum. What is the most appropriate initial suspicion?
explanation: A chronic cough lasting over two weeks accompanied by hemoptysis and weight loss strongly points toward pulmonary tuberculosis. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h3)

question: What major advantage does the GeneXpert test have over standard sputum smear microscopy?

options.A: It does not require any biological sample collection
options.B: It can be performed instantly without electricity anywhere
options.C: It is completely painless because it uses blood samples only
options.D: It detects bacterial DNA and rifampicin resistance rapidly

explanation: GeneXpert is a molecular test that simultaneously confirms TB and checks for resistance to rifampicin within hours. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is Ziehl-Neelsen sputum microscopy referred to as an acid-fast test?

options.A: The test only works when the patient's stomach acid levels are very high
options.B: The bacteria retain the stain even after being washed with an acid-alcohol solution
options.C: The chemical stain used is entirely composed of liquid organic acids
options.D: The sputum sample must be mixed with strong acid before it can be viewed

explanation: Mycobacteria possess a waxy cell wall that resists decolorization by acid-alcohol, earning them the name acid-fast bacilli. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the Directly Observed Therapy (DOTS) strategy?

options.A: To ensure the patient swallows every dose of medication to prevent drug resistance
options.B: To provide free nutritional food packs directly to the patient's home
options.C: To measure lung capacity changes weekly during treatment
options.D: To test the patient's blood pressure twice daily at the clinic

explanation: DOTS ensures adherence so patients do not miss doses, which prevents the development of drug-resistant strains of tuberculosis. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is tuberculosis treated with a combination of multiple drugs rather than just a single antibiotic?

options.A: To prevent the bacteria from easily developing drug resistance
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing the medications
options.C: To make the treatment finish within a single week
options.D: To prevent common stomach upsets caused by single drugs

explanation: Using multiple drugs with different mechanisms ensures that any naturally resistant mutants are killed by the other agents in the regimen. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which anti-TB medication is known to cause harmless orange-red discoloration of body fluids?
explanation: Rifampicin naturally turns urine, sweat, and tears an orange-red color, and nurses must counsel patients beforehand to prevent panic. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h6)

question: A patient on tuberculosis treatment reports that their urine has turned bright orange and wants to stop taking the drugs. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Suggest drinking large amounts of palm oil to flush out the colored substance
options.B: Explain that this is a normal, harmless side effect of rifampicin and treatment must continue
options.C: Tell the patient to switch to taking only herbal remedies instead
options.D: Advise the patient to stop all medications immediately and come to the clinic

explanation: Reassuring the patient prevents unwarranted discontinuation of a life-saving medication regimen. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which type of respiratory protection is recommended for healthcare workers caring for patients with active pulmonary TB?
explanation: N95 respirators filter out tiny airborne droplets containing Mycobacterium tuberculosis, protecting the wearer from inhalation. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is maximizing natural ventilation considered a key environmental control against TB transmission?

options.A: It cools down the hospital room to a freezing temperature where bacteria die
options.B: It completely kills all bacteria instantly using fresh oxygen molecules
options.C: It dilutes and disperses infectious airborne droplet nuclei in the room
options.D: It prevents patients from coughing while waiting for their appointments

explanation: Good airflow and ventilation reduce the concentration of infectious aerosols in indoor spaces, lowering the risk of inhalation. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h7)
